text_fidelity_a:
LEGO Disney Mulan’s Storybook Adventures 43174 Creative Building Kit, New 2020 (124 Pieces) As a child, I loved pop-up books, so of course I love all of the LEGO pop-up book building kits. The first one (see [[ASIN:B07GYB8D34 LEGO Pop-Up Book]] originated as a fan model submitted to the LEGO Ideas fan-voting site (if you want to participate, just google for LEGO Ideas). This DISNEY MULAN’S STORYBOOK ADVENTURES 43174 BUILDING KIT (New 2020 (124 Pieces)) is a smaller, simpler version of the original pop-up book, but it’s still a lot of fun.

The basic pop-up feature is the arched bridge that goes from the center--the book’s stationary spine, where Mulan’s buildings are--to the little “tea service” island in the left half of the book. The bridge goes up and down on a LEGO hinge, and snaps into place when the book is completely open.

There are LEGO studs strategically placed around the open book, so that the three dolls, Mulan’s pony, and Mulan’s cricket cage can all be firmly attached at once. This way, they don’t rattle around loose (or get lost) when the book is closed to be put away. When the book is open for play, the dolls fit on the bridge, under the arches, and can stand anywhere on the book surface.

The assembly instructions are reasonably easy to follow--just look closely at the pictures. I had to take my book covers apart and reassemble them because I got the left (blue water) and right (white land) sides switched, so that the water was on the wrong side when the book was opened.

There are quite a few stickers, but only a few that need to be carefully placed on LEGO elements. The instructions aren’t terribly clear on where to place the stickers that go onto the book’s interior surfaces (e.g., the swimming Koi fish, the lily pads, Mulan’s bed roll, the campfire, the cooking supplies). You can consult the box photos, or even the photos in the online LEGO Shop, if you want extra guidance for these.

One of my favorite features is the two little tassels or bells that swing from Mulan’s temple-like building. I don’t know whether this is an entirely new LEGO element, or whether it has appeared in other sets, but it was new to me. There are enough LEGO pieces in the set to make the book interesting to assemble; and the book is fun to play with after it’s built.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Disney Mulan’s Storybook Adventures 43174 Creative Building Kit, New 2020 (124 Pieces)

text_fidelity_a:
Niya - a game by Bruno Cathala I love to play games! Over the years we've played lots of party games and games for groups (may have something to do with having 6 kids), but now that we are empty nesters we have been looking for games for 2 players. We got this at a local games store and we absolutely love it!
I don't particularly like games that are super complex, where you have to read every card and figure out how it interacts with the other 200 cards. Niya can be explained in 5 minutes and played in 10-15 minutes, but it is also strategic.
The quality is excellent, with a great metal tin instead of a cardboard box, sturdy board pieces, and weighty playing pieces.
The artwork is very nice, with a clean, simple aesthetic. Very Japanese!
I have two very nit picky complaints about it. One of the categories on the board pieces is pines. They look very much like cacti to me. The other is that on the black pieces the black hair of the characters kind of disappears. I wish they had outlined them somehow.
All in all a great game. Highly recommended.
text_fidelity_b: Niya - a game by Bruno Cathala

Faber-Castell How to Rainbow Watercolor Pencils Set - Kids Painting Kits, Art Kit for Kids 6-8+ At the time of this review, this set is under $10. If it were over $10, I would probably subtract a star. This is definitely beginner, student quality.
But if you have a child, or maybe you are just looking for something reasonably priced to see if you enjoy sketching, even though it's geared for children, this set can't be beat.

The main reason it gets five stars, is that you get four different hardness levels of graphite pencils. Perfect for experimenting with your creativity and making a sketch come alive. And it's less messy than charcoal sticks, so once again, it's the perfect introduction to nurture a child's creativity and talent.
To make it even better, there's a little pamphlet to encourage and explain how to get your feet wet. I really like that the emphasis is on the fact that there are no mistakes, that each line is is just fine. So important for children that might be discouraged that they aren't instantly a great artist, forgetting or not understanding that being an artist is only 10% talent and 90% learning and desire.
It might be only a folded over page, but it covers various techniques. All is written in a way that kids and young adults can easily follow. This set is cured for ages 7 and up.
And once again, a 7-year-old doesn't need professional quality pencil sharpeners or paper. You can see in the photograph how thin the paper pages are, and how cheesy the little pencil sharpener is. Cheesy, but perfect for the purpose.

This well thought out set is just what I would expect from Farber-Castell. Their supplies are favored by the students and professionals worldwide.

I hope that this review has helped you to make a decision about whether or not this set is right for you or a special child. Kids seem to be passionate about something one minute, and totally change the next. This little set is a very small investment, but of course, little investments add up.

text_fidelity_a:
Crayola Glow Book Seeing commercials for the Glow Book, I've been interested in this toy for my 9 year old. Obviously commercials are made to show the absolute best of a product, so I expected it to be much less than what was advertised. I have to admit it's almost as cool as the advertisements. However, the best way to discover if a toy is really worth it is to test it out on more than just a few kids. I went with those who were interested in art. Thus, this is judging based on kids who are already fans of art.

Honest opinions from kids:

1. It came with pages you could trace for kids who can't draw too well.
2. If you make a mistake, it's easy to erase it, but it's hard to make it all clean. You really have to rub well to erase mistakes or it leaves smearing behind. They should have something to erase it better. At least you can use it more than one time.
3. It needs more pages. You have plastic pages you draw on and the lights come on to show each page. It makes everything look like it's moving when the lights flash. The pages also aren't very straight.
4. I really like to play with the glow book because it is fun. You just have to get used to using it.
5. It was just like a movie. I could color and draw it just how I pleased.
6. It would be nice if there could be just a little more colors because it shows purple in some of the tracings, but there is no purple. Maybe some black to show outlines, too. It just comes with six colors: tan, pink, yellow, blue, red and green.

From an adult's perspective - it definitely has keep the interest going with the kids. It's not a toy that ends up on the shelf - lost and forgotten. However, the price tag is a bit high for something that's so simple. I have seen Amazon have excellent deals on the Glow Book, however, and think if you are patient and give yourself time to find a great deal, you will. Anything less than $20 would be great. I agree with one of the children that it could use more colors. Especially when dealing with kids interested in art. For younger kids, the small amount of color choices is probably fine. Glass cleaner takes care of the smudges you'll find after repeated use by kids. After a few mistakes, the drawing takes on a foggy/dusty look - thus making it harder to see the pictures "move" clearly. Downside is it can't be cleaned until the child is entirely finished. Definitely stick with the manufacturer age recommendation of 6 years and up. This toy is not made well enough to handle rough use from younger kids.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola Glow Book

text_fidelity_a:
Logo Board Game For what it is, a trivia game just based on popular brands, this is probably as good as it gets.

The gameplay is simple, and they've devised a way to play with only using cards and the board, so no die required. The board is a path made up of 4 colors that the instructions say are in 'random' order. And even though the random order would never pass any randomness tests, it makes for game play that moves along.

The cards are the best part. Each card is usually dedicated to a different brand, so you could just thumb through the cards and pick your favorite brands by the pictures on the faces of the cards.

And, you'll probably wonder, since playing this is really similar to watching a couple hours of commercials, "Shouldn't they be paying me to play this game?"

Pros:
+Tons of trivia about tons of different companies
+You can play without dice, so this will last a lot longer than most board games
+Both easy and hard trivia questions, so people don't feel too stupid
+Even if you are really bad at trivia, this game will only take about an hour to play (15 minutes if you're awesome)

Cons:
-All the standard cons that go along with a trivia game. It makes the smart people feel smarter, and the dumb people feel dumber. I'm pretty dumb at trivia, so it was nice to play a trivia game and only feel mildly dumb.
text_fidelity_b: Logo Board Game

text_fidelity_a:
Harry Potter Lexicon-GO! Word Game Lexicon Go is a very fast-paced, easy-to-play word game using a deck of 52 plastic tiles, each with a letter of the alphabet. the tiles are arranged face down on the playing area, and each player draws 10 tiles from the deck. The goal is to arrange all 10 of your tiles into words as quickly as possible. If you're unable to use all of your letters to make words, you can swap out a tile (within certain parameters) or you can play on other players' words. The first player to use all 10 tiles wins the round. Win five rounds and you've won the game.

We played this game with two, three, four, and five adult players. I would guess that in at least 8 out of 10 rounds, one player was able to use all of her letters to form words without any swapping out or playing on another player's tiles -- which made the game move very, very quickly, , but also made it a little bit boring. There is very little strategizing and interaction. The best part was challenging words and learning the meaning of funny new words.

This was a little bit too fast-paced and frenetic for my tastes, and whether you could use all your tiles on the first draw depended primarily on getting a good vowel to consonant ratio- if you draw at least three vowels, it's pretty easy to make two, three, or four letter words to use all ten tiles. If you draw only one or two vowels, you will have a tough time using all your tiles.

The game is fun, clever, and well-made. The carrying case is well-made and the tiles are nice quality. This would be a great family game or vacation game, and it worked equally well with two players as it did with five players -- it just worked differently. It is versatile. If you're a fan of Scrabble or the New York Times crossword, this seems very fast-paced and a little too easy. It may better suited for younger players -- maybe elementary school-aged children.
text_fidelity_b: Harry Potter Lexicon-GO! Word Game

text_fidelity_a:
Ravensburger Zodiac 270 Piece Puzzle Ball I'm someone who will cheat at something if I can. Like when I was was a kid, and I played [[ASIN:B00000IWCT Monopoly]] with my little brothers, I would steal money from the bank, just because I could.

Each piece of this puzzle has a number on the back of it, and the numbers tell you which pieces fit together. So, it's much easier to flip over all of the pieces of the puzzle, and put it together upside down, that by putting the puzzle together by the picture. And it's much easier by a lot. I think that everyone who does this puzzle will eventually get frustrated, and resort to doing the puzzle upside down, which I consider 'cheating.'

It's very solid, and very strong, when you put it together. The pieces are made of sturdy plastic, not cardboard, like other puzzles. Also the pieces seem like they're cast, or molded, and not cut. That's why the globe surface ends up smooth. But, because all of the pieces were manufactured separately, instead as a whole puzzle, then the picture doesn't always match up from piece to piece.

It comes with a cheap stand, but it looks pretty nice when it's assembled and displayed. I hid a few coins in the middle of it, so it rattles when you move it. It's got lot of area in the middle for a small sphere, so it could double as a secret safe.

Pros:
+Very sturdy, especially when the sphere is completed
+Nice picture, with a bunch of cool zodiac symbols
+High quality

Cons:
-Has numbers on the back of each piece of the puzzle, so it's super simple to assemble
-Plastic, so it doesn't feel like a real puzzle
-The picture doesn't always line up from piece to piece
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Zodiac 270 Piece Puzzle Ball

Overall, I found this to be a fun little kit to put together, even though I'm not exactly a car guy. One of the models looks like a traditional black Lamborghini, while the other looks almost like an SUV in comparison, but it's probably jus the scale and the boxiness of the LEGO kits that makes me think this. In addition, you get a starting line that shifts left and right to give you green or red lights, which is a nice little added benefi.

The ads for this one talk about racing the cars, but it's all imaginary - there's no pull-back action or anything like you can get in Tecnic models - and the two included minifigs are basic to the point of being disappointing. Most of the pieces in this one are very small, and there's not much movement in the final models at all. Many of the other bigger pieces have decals, so there's limited use in terms of using this to build other models.

If you have a little car fan at home, this will thrill them. We're not car people, so we thought it was only just a bit better than OK.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Speed Champions Lamborghini Urus ST-X and Lamborghini Huracán Super Trofeo EVO 76899 Building Kit (663 Pieces)

text_fidelity_a: Lifetime Heavy Duty A-Frame Metal Swing Set I absolutely love this swingset. We ordered it from Costco, because the price was a bit lower. We already had the matching jungle gym, so we didn't really want to get the larger monkey bar swingset. I found this one and thought it was perfect. I was right. Assembly was a bear. Based solely on the weight of the pieces, you need a few people to put this together. It takes some maneuvering to get the pieces together and in place, but once they are together, they are solid. The swings and ring were a bit high for my 4 year old, so we picked up four 6 inch sections of chain from the local hardware store and some quick links. Problem solved. We left one of the swings higher for the older kids. My son and I swing on it together, and it only moves a bit. We will likely anchor it in the future, but for small children, it stays in place well enough. The coating on the swings is much better than the normal covered chains which crack and come apart. This is thick rubbery substance that fully wraps around the chains. We didn't use the feet on the bottom as it allows the set to settle into the ground a bit as we use it. The set looks professional, not tacky, and unlike wood sets, I won't be out there trying to clean it and check for splinters constantly. I can see this being used for generations. Great item. Seems like commercial quality.
text_fidelity_b: Lifetime Heavy Duty A-Frame Metal Swing Set

We've played twice with this kit since getting it, and we still have equipment left for making more. The markers themselves are small, and they won't last all that long, but long enough for plenty of use. Everything is very good in terms of quality of components, and ease of making the markers.

One small gripe: making your own colors (i.e. combinations that are not on the helpful color-making sheet they include) is likely going to be a fail. text_fidelity_a: Wit's End Game, A Challenging Trivia and Brain-Teasing Board Game That Tests Players Wits as Well as Their Knowledge. Classic Party Night Fun for Adults and Family. Ages 16+ If those in your family and friend group are the kind of people that watch documentaries and go to museums for fun, this might be your sort of game. The questions rely a lot on having random knowledge on a wide variety of topics, although those with a broad knowledge of science might have an advantage. But the questions also ask about history, geography, literature, art, broadway musicals, economics and sports. The Teaser questions are fun if you like riddles, just don’t overthink it. The game board is simple to figure out but fun to play. The questions definitely make you think, and are fun if you like a challenge. It does some incredible things and any child (with the help of an adult most likely), teen, or adult will love building and driving this little vehicle around using it's remote.

It says it is easy to assemble but just in case you are like we are around here you'll be happy to know it comes with detailed tutorials which include video instructions, schematic diagram and a source code. They come in handy! It has a lot of interesting parts and electronic components that would take me a while to tell you about and that I think you would do better reading up above. It also uses infrared to follow lines in front of it, to avoid things in front of it, and also to follow objects. It's a really fun car.
I think almost anyone that enjoys cars and building things and all that stuff will really have fun with this. The kit is filled with the tools all the tools you need and there is no welding or anything required. It's fun, semi-easy, and so worth it when you get to play with the finished product!

text_fidelity_a:
Escape Room in a Box: Flashback, Escape Room Game with 19 Puzzles and 4 Locks, Can Pair with Amazon Alexa, For Adults and Teens 13 Years Old and Up It's an 80s themed box, with a name like "Flashback" that has nothing to do with the 80s, and very little to do with "flashbacks". It's actually about werewolves, a magic ring, and bad poetry. The story makes no sense at all, and that's the easiest element of an escape room, really. Fortunately, everything else in this box is pretty good.

We played with a group of 4 people, which was perfect. You could even do six and have a great time with it. The game is broken into three paths - red, purple and blue, each with a very vague theme like "poems" (blue), "childhood" (purple) and "dinosaurs" (red) - and you need to complete all three in order to win. We broke our group of four into two teams of two and tackled blue and purple envelopes separately, then worked together on the red and the final puzzle. Each envelope took us roughly the same amount of time to beat, and the final puzzle was appropriately paced to be solved quickly. Most other escape room games we've played, from Unlock to Exit to Escape the Room all suffer from pacing problems, or narrowing you down to having only one puzzle or a few cards to work with at one time, which is nice for pointing out the way to solve some more complex puzzles, but which makes it rather difficult to play with more than two people - this box has solved that problem.

Overall, we were pretty impressed with this with a few caveats. One of the puzzles requires you to do something to the game pieces that is spelled out early on in the letter. It wasn't difficult to figure out what to do, but it was difficult to execute. It's hard to say more without giving out spoilers for one of the "coolest" puzzles in the box, but let's just say that it was mechanically difficult to work with. One of the puzzles at the end of the game required another outside prop that's easy to deal with, but the amount of finagleing with the pieces and the prop left us questioning if we had solved that puzzle correctly (we did, but it wasn't quite clear).

One touch that I particularly liked was how the game color-coded everything according to the paths/envelopes, and how the locked boxes worked - they performed exacly as they should have, and they were high enough quality that we felt like we could toss them around a little without any issues.

This is expensive for a one-time-use product, but it's definitely my favorite of the escape room games for a medium to large sized group, and it's probably pretty good for two slueths to solve on their own as well.

Solved in 1:07:11.
text_fidelity_b: Escape Room in a Box: Flashback, Escape Room Game with 19 Puzzles and 4 Locks, Can Pair with Amazon Alexa, For Adults and Teens 13 Years Old and Up

PAI TECHNOLOGY Botzees Easy-to-Build 6-in-1 Coding Robots for Kids with Puzzles, Augmented Reality STEM Toy, Ages 4,5,6,7,8,9,10+ Year Old Boys and Girls (App Based) I gave this PAI TECHNOLOGY Botzees Building and Coding - Construction Kit with Puzzles, Augmented Reality to my 7 year old son as a gift from Santa. In comparison to other robot building kits, I wasn't that impressed. First of all, you MUST have an updated iOs or Android phone/tablet. I am unsure if Android has this problem, but if you have an iPhone 5 or 6 and you can't update to the latest iOs, you will not be able to use this robot. Also, since this is an augmented reality app, I doubt that the Kindle Fire will work on this. The camera just isn't powerful enough. I ran into this problem with my son's Fire HD 10 for other AR programs. Next, when you unbox, there are no instructions. You have to go a website to get the instruction manual, which could have been printed on the two cards in the box that say go to the website for a manual. Finally, this does not come with a power source. There is a lithium battery and a USB cable, but you will have to have your own plug. Obviously, many of us will already have various plugs, but to have a designated plug would be nice considering the amount asked for this product.

Overall, my son's interest in this was limited. He's much more interested using his other building toys and finding ways for them to move. I think he feels limited in his creativity. You cannot use this without the App, so any ideas he has of incorporating other mediums to this has him frustrated. It's a nice idea. However, considering that I try to limit his screen time as well it would be nice to have an off screen option to play with this.
text_fidelity_b: PAI TECHNOLOGY Botzees Easy-to-Build 6-in-1 Coding Robots for Kids with Puzzles, Augmented Reality STEM Toy, Ages 4,5,6,7,8,9,10+ Year Old Boys and Girls (App Based)

Educational Insights GeoSafari Fossil Excavation Kit, Kids Science Kit, Dinosaur Science Toy, Ages 7+ All of the fossils were in a single spot, and it took only a second to find them. I soaked the block in water, as I didn't want to take hours to dig them out, and after a little bit, I was able to pull the fossils out of the block with ease. I got this kit specifically for the trilobite, as I have always wanted one and didn't have one yet. So imagine my dismay when my new trilobite is crumbling to pieces in front of me. It couldn't have been damaged by my not digging correctly, as I didn't even dig at all.

I looked it over and I was upset to find spots that had been glued together. That tells me they knew it was coming apart when they included it. I guess they thought it was going to go to a kid who would just assume they broke it by being careless and would just throw it out and not care, but I personally don't like that they included a piece that was crumbling. There are other reviews that have the same problem with their trilobite crumbling and there are also others with pictures of the same.

The other fossils are all fine, and if you don't care at all about the trilobite, then I guess this kit is still ok to get. But I can't bring myself to recommend it to anyone because they knowingly included a broken and glued back together fossil.

AKAMATE Kids Action Camera Waterproof Video Digital Children Cam 1080P HD Sports Camera Camcorder for Boys Girls, Build-in 4Games, 32GB SD Card [[VIDEOID:3ab25a1fe74e640fbb16d3764ecc8aea]] This Kid's Action Camera was better than I expected. The camera (not in the waterproof case) measures 2.5" tall x 2.25" wide x 7/8" thick. The full color screen on the back measures 1.5" tall x 1.25" wide. The photographs can be up to 5M (you select can 5M, 3M, 2M, or 1M), and the photographs actually look pretty good (good color balance, no distortion, in focus). You can record just audio, and this came out clear when the camera was held within a foot distance of my mouth. I didn't test any further. The video can be selected at 1080P, 720P, or VGA quality. The 1080P looked good but it doesn't appear to be the normal HD proportions but rather closer to a square than a long rectangle. Some of the recordings also had mysterious sounds in addition to the expected ones--maybe like something tapped against the case during the recording. Also, I haven't found a way to remove the automatic time stamp placed on the video and photos. You can playback the videos, etc. on the camera if desired and also delete them off if the take was a bad one.

I found the camera very easy to use once I read the instructions. One rechargeable Li-ion battery is included. You charge the battery using the included USB cord connected to a computer or using a USB charging adapter. There's a red LED light when charging which turns off when it's full. Charging didn't take long, and they estimate that a full charge from near empty will take about 2.5 hours. I did notice that, even with the camera switched off in addition to being turned off, the battery tends to drain. We used the camera a bit, then left it sitting for a few weeks, only to discover that it needed to be fully recharged before we could use it again. So just charge it periodically so it'll always have enough of a charge.

They estimate that you can take about 90 minutes of 1080P video on the included 32 GB micro SD card (probably limited by the battery as I think 32GB can hold twice that). You need to format the micro SD card before use. You can do this by inserting the card into the camera, going to the settings menu, and selecting the option to format the card. You can download the images, audio, and video from the camera either through the USB cable (turn the camera on before connecting to your computer) or by removing the micro SD card and inserting it in the destination computer.

The set includes connectors that allow you to connect the camera to connectors that attach to a helmet, a bike, and so on. In the instructions, they show how the various connectors can be used for different situations. The set also comes in a very nice storage / carrying case so the unused connectors and such don't get lost. There is a holder for the camera that is a waterproof shell (good up to 30m or 98 feet underwater) and this can also be connected to all these other connectors.

I tried to film a sunset, and it did look pretty accurate when the lens was pointed directly at the sun/brightest area. If I dropped the focus of the camera to the ground, the camera Auto changed things so that it looked like a bright daylight scene. I tried some video of moving objects (like a flag on a windy day) or with me moving the camera, and it came out good.

The 3 games were pretty simple and may bore kids used to touchscreens. For example, the puzzle game would be pretty quick to work except you have to select a piece, use the arrow to move it one square, then select a piece, etc. Lots of clicking the buttons. Still, fun if there aren't other options around.
text_fidelity_b: AKAMATE Kids Action Camera Waterproof Video Digital Children Cam 1080P HD Sports Camera Camcorder for Boys Girls, Build-in 4Games, 32GB SD Card

Venn Board Game | Family Game for 2+ Players | Cooperative & Competitive Gameplay Variations | Creative Word Association Game Featuring Unique Gameplay & Custom Artwork | Ages 10+ Venn is a party game that plays a large number of players, and it comes with a competitive mode and a cooperative mode. The cooperative mode was not fun for our family, so we'll focus on the competitive game. In this game, you use cards with odd artwork to get your teammates to guess a set of three out of twelve possible games. The cards go in one of the seven different sections of a three-way Venn Diagram like you used to see in school. Using the clues you're given, you attempt to identify the three chosen words that the card placer is going for.

There are some fun times to be had here, but a few problems as well. The art is meant to be odd and unusual, but a good amount of it is just plain bad - characters are off-center, objects look like they're floating in the background, etc - and the cards are hard to use because they don't actually fit inside the sections of the Venn diagram. The words are usually very descriptive, but there are also some bad word chocies in the deck like "great" or "interesting" which could literally mean anything.

Unfortunately, this is competing in a crowded market - competitive, team-based family games have been done to death, so if you want to stand out, choose a game like Codenames or Just One or So Clover or...well, there's a lot of them, and they're mostly better than this.
text_fidelity_b: Venn Board Game | Family Game for 2+ Players | Cooperative & Competitive Gameplay Variations | Creative Word Association Game Featuring Unique Gameplay & Custom Artwork | Ages 10+

Man, that was a fun and FAST hour!  I have grandkids and got this for my son and his two kids and whoever else has the stamina to go the distance with them - I have a younger son and daughter-in-law that love to play with their niece and nephew so it's usually one of them.  The only thing is, I had to buy another large container of rechargeable AA batteries.  OMG, these require a total of 28 AA batteries!  And just so you don't run out in the middle of an especially contentious battle, you BETTER have another 28 AA batteries charged and ready...whew, that's a LOT of batteries!  Oh well...better to plan for a fun day than to wimp out, right?  Now when everyone is a bit tuckered out from running around shooting at each other, they can switch to drone strikes with someone flying a drone and another one shooting it down.  Not bad!  I may end up purchasing another set (and whole bunch more batteries) so both my sons, both my daughters-in-law, and my grandkids can play at the same time - big kids and little kids running around, squealing and laughing.  For me, that's better than TV!  I took one star off just for the massive amounts of batteries you need.  Too bad the people who created this didn't think to make these USB rechargeable.

The truck looks realistic with nice details inside the cab with a center console, two bucket seats, a dashboard and a steering wheel.  It is molded in 4 colors plus a clear plastic windshield, sunroof and back window.  The side doors have no windows.  The steering wheel turns, but is not functional for turning the wheels.  The two front doors of the truck both open.  The hood of the truck opens to reveal an engine.  Nice detail including non-functioning headlights, parking lights, front grill, side mirrors, gas cap and a rear tailgate that also opens.  The only assembly required on the truck is putting on the 4 tires, which should be easy for just about any kid.  The horse trailer also requires putting on 4 tires and a special wheel in the front; also there are 6 trailer pieces that have to be snapped in place. An illustrated book shows how to install the pieces.  Pretty easy, but a younger child might have a little trouble figuring it out.  The pictures on the side of the trailer and the license plates on the truck and trailer are provided in a sheet of stickers, which a child can place where they like.  Includes a completely black horse with a blanket, 2 figures (a driver for the truck and a handler for the horse) and several accessories for the horse including a bridle, halter, saddle, a couple brushes, a bale of hay and a bunch of carrots.  Suitable for both boys or girls, especially those who like horses.  Probably this toy would be preferred by girls since the truck is pink and the horse handler is female. Even some adult collectors might like this set as it is colorful, detailed and well made. The real downside that I see to this set is that if you have very young children who will be around this, they could easily put one of the small pieces in their mouth and choke.  There is no instructions on showing how to use the horse accessories; most are obvious, but a couple are not.  The most important thing to know is that this is more of an "old school" type of toy; no batteries, no motors, no remotes.  A lot of kids today want the latest electronic devices and radio controlled toys, but this toy allows them to use their imaginations a little. I think that's a plus, but if you buy this for the kid who wants a cell phone instead, there will be a level of disappointment, I'm sure.  Note that this is made by a German company, with components from Germany, China, Romania and Tunisia. It's not that important to me where it is made, but it might be to you.  Note too that you can also buy other items in this series, such as a barn type structure, a corral and other horses.  If your child insists on other components, it could get expensive, if you give in.  As a kid at heart, I like this toy a lot myself and would keep it if I didn't have so many other things.  It will probably go to a grandson.
text_fidelity_b: Schleich Horse Club, 15-Piece Playset, Horse Toys for Girls and Boys 5-12 years old Pick Up with Horse Box

text_fidelity_a: Holy Stone HS170 Predator Mini RC Helicopter Drone 2.4Ghz 6-Axis Gyro 4 Channels Quadcopter Good Choice for Drone Training This is a fun little drone and well worth the money. It is very quick and agile yet easy to control. I strongly suggest to read the instructions first before flight and get familiar with the controls.  It's easy once you figure it out and know what does what. Flying indoors is a bit of a challenge until you get a hold of it but outdoors it zips around like a hummingbird. It has headless mode which makes controlling it easier but it beeps while in headless mode.  It does not have alt hold so it won't hover in one level spot so you stay fully engaged with this during flight. The battery gets about 6-7 minutes. It's so light that a strong breeze will effect it outdoors but it can hold its own quite well. The prop guards and feet are pretty good for cushioning any crashes. Overall a very inexpensive but well built drone that is just a lot of fun to fly.
